General raster read and convert

Source: R/00_warpgeneral.R
gdal_raster_data.Rd

The warper is used to convert source/s to an output file or to data in memory.

Usage

gdal_raster_data(
  dsn,
  target_crs = NULL,
  target_dim = NULL,
  target_ext = NULL,
  target_res = NULL,
  resample = "near",
  bands = 1L,
  band_output_type = NULL,
  options = character(),
  include_meta = TRUE,
  unscale = TRUE,
  open_options = NULL
)

gdal_raster_dsn(
  dsn,
  target_crs = NULL,
  target_dim = NULL,
  target_ext = NULL,
  target_res = NULL,
  resample = "near",
  bands = NULL,
  band_output_type = NULL,
  options = character(),
  out_dsn = tempfile(fileext = ".tif"),
  include_meta = TRUE,
  open_options = NULL
)

gdal_raster_image(
  dsn,
  target_crs = NULL,
  target_dim = NULL,
  target_ext = NULL,
  target_res = NULL,
  resample = "near",
  bands = NULL,
  band_output_type = NULL,
  options = character(),
  include_meta = TRUE,
  open_options = NULL
)

gdal_raster_nara(
  dsn,
  target_crs = NULL,
  target_dim = NULL,
  target_ext = NULL,
  target_res = NULL,
  resample = "near",
  bands = NULL,
  band_output_type = NULL,
  options = character(),
  include_meta = TRUE,
  open_options = NULL
)

Arguments

dsn

data sources, files, urls, db strings, vrt, etc

target_crs

projection of the target grid

target_dim

dimension of the target grid

target_ext

extent of the target grid

target_res

resolution of the target grid

resample

resampling algorithm used

bands

band or bands to include (1-based), may be repeated or in any order, or NULL for all bands. The default is the first band only, see Details for the image functions

band_output_type

specify the band type, see vapour_read_raster

options

general options passed to gdal warper

include_meta

metadata is attached, turn off by setting this to FALSE

unscale

default is TRUE so values are converted by the band's scale and offset to floating point, set to FALSE to get the stored values. An integer band_output_type also gives the stored values, see vapour_read_raster

open_options

open options for the driver, a character vector of "NAME=VALUE" strings (as -oo in the GDAL command line tools), NULL for none. These apply when each source is opened, "-oo" pairs found in options are treated the same way

out_dsn

file name for output "_dsn"

Value

pixel values in a list vector per band, or a list of file paths

Details

Two functions 'gdal_raster_data' and 'gdal_raster_dsn' act like the gdalwarp command line tool, a convenience third function 'gdal_raster_image()' works especially for image data.

For gdal_raster_image() and gdal_raster_nara() the default bands = NULL means the first bands up to four, which is what an image can use. gdal_raster_dsn() writes every band, use vapour_vrt() on the source to choose bands for it.

Examples

dsn <- system.file("extdata/sst.tif", package = "vapour")
## do nothing, get native
X <- gdal_raster_data(dsn)

## set resolution (or dimension, extent, crs, or combination thereof - GDAL 
## will report/resolve incompatible opts)
X1 <- gdal_raster_data(dsn,  target_res = 1)

## add a cutline, and cut to it using gdal warp args

if (interactive()) {
 cutline <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
 wkt <- "POLYGON ((142 -41, 149 -41, 146 -58, 142 -41))"
 write.csv(data.frame(id = 1, WKT = wkt), cutline, row.names = FALSE)
 X1c <- gdal_raster_data(dsn,  target_res = .5, 
     options = c("-cutline",cutline, "-crop_to_cutline"))
 file.remove(cutline)
}

## warp whole grid to given res
X2 <- gdal_raster_data(dsn,  target_res = 25000, target_crs = "EPSG:32755")

## specify exactly (as per vapour originally)
X3 <- gdal_raster_data(dsn,  target_ext = c(-1, 1, -1, 1) * 8e6, 
 target_dim = c(512, 678), target_crs = "+proj=stere +lon_0=147 +lat_0=-90")
 
X4 <- gdal_raster_dsn(dsn, out_dsn = tempfile(fileext = ".tif"))
